_README.what_this_is: The partner-health composite score's weights and normalisation bounds. These are OUR DESIGN DECISION, not a scheme parameter and not a transcribed figure — so they are labelled 'design_decision' rather than left null. They are in a data file, and exported to the UI, because ROADMAP §7 requires the score to be transparent and defensible rather than clever.
_README.deliberately_not_a_model: There is no training data for partner performance, so a learned score would be unexplainable and strictly worse than four weights we can justify on stage. Do not replace this with a model.
_README.formula: health = w_fund_availability·fund_availability_norm + w_npa·(1 − npa_norm) + w_overdue·(1 − overdue_norm) + w_speed·speed_norm
_README.invariant: The four weights must sum to exactly 1. tests/health.weights.test.ts asserts this.
_README.note_on_bounds: Normalisation bounds turn raw figures into 0..1. They are judgement calls about what 'bad' looks like, and changing them changes the ranking — which is exactly why they live here in the open and not inside the scoring function.

capacity_note: CLOSED multiplies the composite to zero rather than hard-filtering the partner out, so the UI can still show the partner with an explanation instead of silently dropping it. Hard filters are reserved for capability, ticket range and jurisdiction — see src/core/partners/match.ts.
verified_note: verified:true here means 'this is genuinely our stated design decision', not 'this came from a guideline'. It is the only file in data/ where that distinction applies.
